# S53 — Create the ork logo

Owner asked for a logo (2026-10-20). Interview answers: an agent drafts hand-written SVG candidates and the owner picks one; the logo is used in the README header, the TUI header or splash, the ork --version and ork doctor banner, and a favicon or repository social image. This slice draws and lands the logo and the README header; S54 uses it in the terminal.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

ork has no mark. The README, the repository page and the terminal all want one, and the owner wants to choose it.

## Files

- assets/logo.svg (the chosen mark), assets/logo-square.svg (square export for a favicon or social image), assets/candidates/ (the drafts, removed or kept as the owner decides), README.md (header), docs/design.md or docs/dashboard.md only if they name the logo.
- The SVG is hand-written plain text: no generator, no new dependency, no raster file, no font that needs installing (text converted to paths or left out).

## Failing tests

- Ask the owner before building: look and feel (name the idea, colours or monochrome, wordmark or glyph), and whether the candidates stay in the repo.
- assets/logo.svg and assets/logo-square.svg are well-formed XML (parsed by a Go test with encoding/xml) with a viewBox, a title, and no script or external reference.
- The logo reads on a light and a dark background (a test checks the SVG sets no background-dependent colour pair that disappears, or ships a dark variant).
- README.md shows the logo at the top with alt text.
- The files carry no copyright claim beyond the repository licence (GPL-3.0-or-later); the owner approves the final choice.
